'''Samuel Davis Dalembert''' (born May 10, 1981) is a Haitian-Canadian former professional [[basketball]] player who played 13 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall University]]. During his active NBA career, Dalembert was known for his [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] as well as his [[Block (basketball)|shot blocking]] ability.

==High school and college career==
Dalembert was born in [[Port-au-Prince]], Haiti and lived there for fourteen years before moving to Montreal, where he attended Lucien-Pagé (High School). He also attended [[St. Patrick High School (New Jersey)|St. Patrick High School]] in [[Elizabeth, New Jersey]]. He then went on to play college basketball at [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] from 1999 to 2001.

==Professional career==
Dalembert was selected with the 26th overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the [[2001 NBA draft]]. After playing 8 seasons with the 76ers, he was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[Andrés Nocioni]] and [[Spencer Hawes]] on June 17, 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5297829 |title=76ers send Dalembert to Kings |work=ESPN.com |date=June 17, 2010|access-date=January 5, 2014}}</ref>

On December 26, 2011, he signed a multi-year deal with the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7390207/samuel-dalembert-signs-multiyear-contract-houston-rockets|title=Rockets sign C Samuel Dalembert|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2011|access-date=December 26, 2011}}</ref>

On June 27, 2012, Dalembert was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], along with [[John Henson (basketball)|John Henson]], the 14th pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]], for [[Jon Brockman]], [[Jon Leuer]], [[Shaun Livingston]], and [[Jeremy Lamb]], the 12th pick in the 2012 NBA draft.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/center-samuel-dalembert-and-14th-draft-pick-highlight-trade-rockets|title=Center Samuel Dalembert and 14th Draft Pick Highlight Trade with Rockets|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2012|access-date=June 27, 2012}}</ref>

On July 19, 2013, Dalembert signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/19/mavs-sign-center-dalembert.ap/|title=Mavericks sign free-agent center Dalembert|date=July 19, 2013|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=July 19, 2013}}</ref>

On June 25, 2014, Dalembert, along with [[Shane Larkin]], [[Wayne Ellington]], [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]] and two 2014 second-round picks, was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Tyson Chandler]] and [[Raymond Felton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire|title=Knicks Acquire Calderon, Three Others in Dallas Trade|date=June 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 25, 2014}}</ref> On January 5, 2015, he was waived by the Knicks.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-part-three-team-trade|title=Knicks Part of Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2015}}</ref>

Dalembert's final NBA game was played on December 27, 2014, in a 129–135 loss to the Sacramento Kings. In his final game, Dalembert recorded 11 points, 4 rebounds and 4 blocks.

On August 6, 2015, Dalembert signed with the Dallas Mavericks, returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-center-samuel-dalembert/|title=Mavericks sign center Samuel Dalembert|work=mavs.com|date=August 6, 2015|access-date=August 6, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Mavericks on October 24 prior to the start of the regular season. He appeared in four preseason games for the team, but a left leg injury forced him to miss the final three games of the preseason schedule.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=18509|title=Mavericks waive Sam Dalembert, Brandon Ashley, Tu Holloway, Jamil Wilson|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 24, 2015|access-date=October 24, 2015}}</ref> On December 17, 2015, he signed with [[Shanxi Zhongyu]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ecns.cn/2015/12-18/192966.shtml|title=NBA player Dalembert joins China's Shanxi Fenjiu|work=Ecns.cn|date=December 18, 2015|access-date=December 18, 2015}}</ref> He returned to Shanxi for the 2016–17 season.

==National team career==
After much anticipation, Dalembert became a [[Canadians|Canadian]] [[citizen]] on August 7, 2007, and joined the [[Canada national men's basketball team|Canadian national team]] in hopes of qualifying for the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/news/story?id=2965344|title=76ers' Dalembert to play for Canada after gaining citizenship|work=ESPN.com|date=August 7, 2007|access-date=August 7, 2007}}</ref> He made his national team debut during the [[2007 FIBA Americas Championship]], leading the tournament with 2.4 blocks per game.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20201116133916/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/statistics/p/sid/3965/sp/ALL/srid/ALL/ss/BL/tid/0/_/2007_FIBA_Americas_Championship/player-leaders.html 2007 FIBA Americas Championship - Player Leaders - Blocks] FIBA.com. Accessed on January 4, 2020.</ref> He also participated in Canada's pre-Olympic qualifying training camp, taking part in games in both [[Toronto]] and [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]] during the 2008 Jack Donohue International Classic, with wins over both [[Lebanon men's national basketball team|Lebanon]] and [[New Zealand national basketball team|New Zealand]]. However, Dalembert was later dismissed from the team during the [[2008 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament for Men|World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]] due to a rift between him and coach [[Leo Rautins]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/chl/story/?id=252456 |title=DALEMBERT: 'I'LL PLAY FOR CANADA BUT NOT FOR RAUTINS' |work=TSN.ca |date=October 12, 2008 |access-date=October 12, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106040208/http://www.tsn.ca/chl/story/?id=252456 |archive-date=January 6, 2014 }}</ref>

==Haiti earthquake==
Dalembert decided to travel to Haiti to help with relief efforts following the [[2010 Haiti earthquake]]. He also pledged $100,000 to [[UNICEF]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/dalembert_donation_100114.html|title=SIXERS CENTER SAMUEL DALEMBERT AND NBA'S ONLY HAITIAN-BORN PLAYER TO PERSONALLY DONATE $100,000 TO UNICEF IN SUPPORT OF HAITIAN RELIEF EFFORTS BEFORE GAME ON FRIDAY, JANUARY 15|work=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2010|access-date=January 14, 2010}}</ref>

He won the 2009–10 J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award for his contributions to Haitian people after the earthquake.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/100419_dalembert.html | title=DALEMBERT WINS 2009-10 J. WALTER KENNEDY CITIZENSHIP AWARD - 4/19/2010 | work=NBA.com | date=April 19, 2010 | access-date=January 5, 2014}}</ref> Since the disaster, Dalembert has continued to be involved in the Haitian recovery.
